parameters.content:
## Newsletter · AI drafting engine
For a chosen date, gathers that day's stored research, proposes the top stories and a subject line, and takes the editor's written feedback on each over Telegram until they approve. It then writes each story from its research and outside sources, adds an intro and a round-up, and sends the editor a draft file with a summary.

**Platforms:** Google Drive, Supabase, Telegram, Gemini, Groq
**Source and tests:** github.com/kimjoshuadr/n8n-workflows · `production/newsletter-drafting`

## 1. Retrieve Markdown content
The research stored for the chosen date, read from Google Drive and joined into one text.

## 2. Pick top stories
A proposal, the reasoning behind it, and the editor's reply. A reply that asks for changes goes round again.

## 3. Subject line
The same loop for the subject line: propose, explain, wait for the editor.

## 4. Write each story
One story per pass: its research, any outside sources, the story, its images.

## 6. Format full newsletter
The round-up, the assembled draft, and delivery as a file with a summary.

parameters.formDescription: Drafts the issue for one date from that day's research.

assignments.name: prompt
assignments.value:
={{ 'Date: ' + $json.date + '
Editor focus: ' + ($json.focus || 'none given') + '
' + ($json.sparse ? 'Only ' + $json.count + ' research documents exist for this date. Choose fewer stories instead of padding: one strong story is enough.' : 'Choose the three or four strongest stories.') + '

Research:
' + $json.research }}

messageValues.message: [task:pick-stories] You are the editor of a daily industry newsletter. Use only what is in the research you are given: never add a fact, a number or a quote that is not there. Choose the top stories for today's issue. For each, give a headline, the ids of the research documents it draws on (the ids in square brackets), any outside links in those documents worth reading in full, and why it leads. Then give your overall reasoning for the selection.

[task:edit-stories] You are the editor of a daily industry newsletter. Use only what is in the research you are given: never add a fact, a number or a quote that is not there. The editor has asked for changes to the story selection. Apply exactly what they asked and keep everything else. Answer in the same shape, with your reasoning for the revised selection.

parameters.message: ={{ 'Reply Approve to go on with these stories, or say what to change.' }}

options.systemPromptTemplate: [task:read-feedback] Read the editor's reply to a proposal. approved is true only when they accept it as it is, with nothing they want changed. Otherwise approved is false and feedback is what they want changed, in their words.

assignments.name: examples
assignments.value: ={{ '- Rates hold, markets shrug\n- The chip that changes the maths\n- Three deals you missed this week' }}

assignments.name: prompt
assignments.value:
={{ 'Stories in this issue:
' + $('set_current_stories').first().json.stories.map((s) => '- ' + s.title + ': ' + s.why).join('
') + '

Subject lines in the house style:
' + $json.examples }}

messageValues.message: [task:subject-line] You are the editor of a daily industry newsletter. Use only what is in the research you are given: never add a fact, a number or a quote that is not there. Write the subject line for this issue in the house style shown: under 50 characters, concrete, no clickbait and no emoji. Add a preheader of under 90 characters and one sentence of reasoning.

[task:edit-subject] You are the editor of a daily industry newsletter. Use only what is in the research you are given: never add a fact, a number or a quote that is not there. The editor has asked for changes to the subject line. Apply exactly what they asked. Answer in the same shape.

parameters.message: ={{ 'Reply Approve to use this subject line, or say what to change.' }}

options.systemPromptTemplate: [task:read-feedback] Read the editor's reply to a proposal. approved is true only when they accept it as it is, with nothing they want changed. Otherwise approved is false and feedback is what they want changed, in their words.

messageValues.message: [task:write-segment] You are the editor of a daily industry newsletter. Use only what is in the research you are given: never add a fact, a number or a quote that is not there. Write one story for the issue: a headline and a body of 120 to 200 words in plain, direct prose. List the addresses of the sources you used.

[task:image-urls] List the addresses of images that appear in this research and belong with the story: charts, product photos, screenshots. Only addresses that are in the text. An empty list is a fine answer.

[task:write-intro] You are the editor of a daily industry newsletter. Use only what is in the research you are given: never add a fact, a number or a quote that is not there. Write the opening of the issue: two or three sentences that greet the reader and say what is in it, in the order the stories appear.

parameters.text:
={{ 'Already covered: ' + $('set_current_stories').first().json.stories.map((s) => s.title).join('; ') + '

Research not yet used:
' + ($('aggregate_markdown_content').first().json.items.filter((d) => !$('set_current_stories').first().json.stories.some((s) => (s.content_ids ?? []).includes(d.content_id))).map((d) => '- ' + d.title + ' (' + d.url + '): ' + String(d.text).slice(0, 600)).join('
') || 'none') }}

messageValues.message: [task:other-stories] You are the editor of a daily industry newsletter. Use only what is in the research you are given: never add a fact, a number or a quote that is not there. From the research that was not chosen as a top story, list up to five items worth a line each: the title, its address and one sentence. If nothing is left, answer with an empty list.

assignments.name: markdown
assignments.value:
={{ '# ' + $('set_current_subject_line').first().json.subject_line + '

' + $('set_current_subject_line').first().json.preheader + '

' + $('write_intro').first().json.output.intro + '

' + $('iterate_stories').all().map((i) => i.json).map((s) => '## ' + s.headline + '

' + s.body + (s.image_urls.length ? '

![](' + s.image_urls[0] + ')' : '') + (s.sources.length ? '

Sources: ' + s.sources.join(', ') : '')).join('

') + (($json.output.items ?? []).length ? '

## Also worth reading

' + $json.output.items.map((o) => '- [' + o.title + '](' + o.url + '): ' + o.line).join('
') : '') }}

assignments.name: summary
assignments.value: ={{ 'Draft for ' + $('submit_form').first().json['Newsletter date'] + ' is attached. Subject line: ' + $('set_current_subject_line').first().json.subject_line + '. ' + $('iterate_stories').all().length + ' stories: ' + $('iterate_stories').all().map((i) => i.json.headline).join('; ') + '. Also worth reading: ' + ($json.output.items ?? []).length + ' items.' }}
